text:
Introduction
⚫ The nervous system controls and monitors human movement by transmitting & receiving signals through an extensive neural network: centralnervoussystem& peripheralnervous system
⚫ Motorneuron: the main signal transmitter which carries the impulse to the muscle
⚫ Sensoryneuron:provides feedback to spinal cord and back to CNS on the characteristics of the muscle or other tissues
⚫ While performing a particular movement, the nervous system is responsible for identifying ⚫ the muscles that will be activated & generating the stimulus to develop the level of force that will be required for that muscle

text:
Introduction
⚫ Each muscle fiber is individually innervatedby a branch of the nervous ⚫ system
⚫ Information exits the muscle & provides input to the nervous system (sensory neuron)
⚫ Information enters the muscle to initiate a muscle activity of a specific nature & magnitude (motor neuron)
⚫ Through this loop system, with many other loops from other muscles & with centralnervous control, the nervous system is able to coordinate the activity of many muscles at once, so particular movements or activities can be performed

text:
Nervous System
⚫ Consists of two parts
1.
1. Central nervous system (CNS)
⚫ Brain, spinal cord
⚫ The means by which human movement is initiated, controlled, and monitored
2. Peripheral nervous system (PNS)
2.
⚫ All the branches of the nerves that lie outside the spinal cord
⚫ The peripheral nerves that responsible for muscularaction are the spinal nerves

text:
Spinal Nerves
⚫ Total 31 pairs of spinal nerves
⚫ Exit & enter the spinal cord at the various vertebral levels
⚫ Cervical region: 8 pairs
⚫ Thoracic region: 12 pairs
⚫ Lumbar region: 5 pairs
⚫ Sacral region: 5 pairs
⚫ Coccygeal region: 1 pair

text:
Spinal Nerves
⚫ Sensoryneurons:the nerves that entering the spinal cord on the dorsal root (posterior)
⚫ Transmit information into the system from the muscle
⚫ Afferent pathway – carries all incoming information
⚫ Motorneurons: the nerves that exiting on the ventralroot (anterior) of the spinal cord
⚫ Carry impulses away from the system to the muscle
⚫ Efferent pathway – carries all outgoing information
⚫ Both dorsal & ventral roots join together as spinal nervesas they exit the spinal cord

text:
Motor Unit
⚫ Skeletal muscle is organized into functional groups called motor units.
⚫ Motorunit:
⚫ consists of a group of muscle fibers that are innervated by the same motorneuron
⚫ From a few muscle fibers or up to 2000 muscle fibers
⚫ When a motor neuron is stimulated enough to cause a contraction, all muscle fibers innervated by that motor neuron contract
⚫ Action potential: the signal to contract that is transmitted from the motor neuron to the muscle
⚫ The action potential from a motor neuron reaches a muscle fiber at motorend plate (neuromuscular junction)

text:
Motor Unit
⚫ The motor unit consists of a motor neuron & all of the muscle fibers innervated by that neuron.
⚫ The motor neurons exit the anterior side of the spinal cord and branch out, terminating on the muscle fibers.

text:
Sensory Receptors
⚫ The body requires an input system to provide feedbackon the condition & changing characteristics of the musculoskeletal system and other body tissues, such as skin
⚫ Sensors collect the following information:
⚫ Stretch in the muscle
⚫ Heat / pressure on the muscle
⚫ Tension in the muscle
⚫ Pain in the extremity

text:
Sensory Receptors
⚫ These sensors send information to the spinal cord
⚫ Information is processed & used by the central nervous system in the adjustment / initiation of motor output to the muscles
⚫ These sensors are connected to the spinal cord via sensory neurons
⚫ When a sensory neuron brings information into the spinal cord and initiates a motor response, it is termed a reflex

Reflex
⚫ Asimple reflex arc
⚫ Sensory information from receptors is sent into the spinal cord
➢ Motor response is sent out to the extremities
➢ e.g. stretch reflex

text:
Proprioceptors
⚫ Proprioceptors
⚫ Mainsensory receptors in the musculoskeletal system
⚫ transform mechanical distortion in the muscle into the nerve impulses that enter the spinal cord & stimulate a motor response
⚫ Examples:
⚫ Muscle spindle: found in belly of the muscle; responds to the change in muscle length or velocity of a muscle stretch
⚫ Golgi tendonorgan(GTO): found in muscle-tendon junction; responds to tension in the muscle
